Claire — thanks for the clear asks. Putting the first pass below and attaching a drawio export.

On the diagram: it shows the minimal hops we recommend for the pilot staging environment:
1) Client -> EdgeCorp LB (staging) -> Redwood ingress proxy (staging)
2) Ingress proxy -> Control plane auth (mTLS) for token validation -> Route to model runtime pool (data-plane)
3) Data-plane runtime nodes read/write KV-cache (local L1 + shared L2 in staging)
4) Telemetry -> Staging observability collector (ingress)

Notes / quick ops checklist (short):
- Ports: allow 443 (mTLS) between EdgeCorp LB and Redwood ingress, allow 10250 for runtime health probes from staging probes only.
- Protocols: TLS 1.3 enforced; control-plane RPC over gRPC with mutual auth.
- Service names to permit (DNS / service account): redwood-ingress.staging, redwood-control.staging, redwood-runtime-{pool}.staging
- KV-cache invalidation rollback: pre-warm a new runtime pool pinned to previous quantization profile; shift 10% traffic for 10m; if errors <0.5% continue ramp; otherwise rollback to pinned pool and clear staging L1 cache.

I've attached: staging-signal-flow.drawio.png (export) — this is the one-page you asked for.

If that looks good, Jonas will add the runbook excerpt with precise probe names and health-check thresholds.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Quick follow-up with concrete operational artefacts (see drive link below).

Runbook excerpt (ops steps):
- Preflight (T-24h): validate cert chain for mTLS on staging LB; confirm routing rule present for redwood-ingress.staging in EdgeCorp routing table; snapshot staging KV-cache metrics.
- Canary (T0): route 1% traffic to new runtime pool; monitor 1m latency P95 and error budget.
- Ramp (T+10m): if P95 <= target and errors <0.5% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 1h windows. Otherwise execute rollback.
- Rollback: change routing back to pinned runtime pool; run cache clear on L1 only; if cache warmup > 5m, consider warm thread prefill.

Health probes and names:
- runtime/liveness (path: /healthz, port: 10250, expect JSON {status:ok})
- runtime/kv-integrity (path: /kv-check, port: 10251, expects sample key read latency < 20ms)

Attachments and evidence: vpc-runbook-v1.pdf (ops runbook excerpt), small tarball of metrics snapshots (metrics-snap-20270509.tgz) are in the shared drive. I added a short checklist doc (HS-123456) in HubSpot for the pilot task.
